         1                 P R O C E E D I N G S

         2                  ACTING PRESIDENT STEWART-COUSINS:

         3       The Senate will please come to order.

         4                  I ask everyone present to rise and

         5       recite with me the Pledge of Allegiance to our

         6       Flag.

         7                  (Whereupon, the assemblage recited

         8       the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.)

         9                  ACTING PRESIDENT STEWART-COUSINS:

        10       In the absence of clergy, may we all bow our

        11       heads for a moment of silence.

        12                  (Whereupon, the assemblage

        13       respected a moment of silence.)

        14                  ACTING PRESIDENT STEWART-COUSINS:

        15       Thank you.

        16                  Senator Smith, I have at the desk

        17       here a proclamation which I am handing down to

        18       the Secretary at this time.

        19                  The Secretary will read.

        20                  THE SECRETARY:    "Proclamation.

        21                  "Pursuant to the power vested in me

        22       by Article IV, Section 3 of the Constitution,

        23       I hereby convene the Senate of the State of

        24       New York in Extraordinary Session at the



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         5431



         1       Capitol, in the City of Albany, on the

         2       twenty-fourth day of June, two thousand nine,

         3       at three o'clock, for the purpose of

         4       considering legislation with respect to

         5       various issues and for the consideration of

         6       legislation with respect to such other

         7       subjects as I may recommend.

         8                  "Given under my hand and the privy

         9       seal of the State, in the City of Albany, this

        10       twenty-third day of June in the year

        11       two thousand nine, by the Governor, David A.

        12       Paterson."

        13                  ACTING PRESIDENT STEWART-COUSINS:

        14       The proclamation having been read, the session

        15       is in extraordinary session.

        16                  Senator Klein.

        17                  SENATOR KLEIN:    Point of order,

        18       Madam President.

        19                  ACTING PRESIDENT STEWART-COUSINS:

        20       Senator Klein, why do you rise?

        21                  SENATOR KLEIN:    My point of

        22       order, Madam President, is regarding legal

        23       concerns about the Senate-only extraordinary

        24       session.



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         5432



         1                  Because the Governor called only

         2       the Senate for an extraordinary session and

         3       not the Assembly, it is questionable that the

         4       bills that the Senate passed could result in

         5       any laws being enacted, even if those bills

         6       contain the same language as bills previously

         7       passed by the Assembly.

         8                  It is clear the Governor has the

         9       power under Article IV, Section 3 of the

        10       Constitution to call only the Senate and leave

        11       the Assembly at home for an extraordinary

        12       session.  However, it is not clear that a

        13       Senate-only extraordinary session can result

        14       in any bills becoming law.

        15                  So the bills that were passed by

        16       the Assembly in regular session that now are

        17       before us in extraordinary session would be

        18       invalid.

        19                  It's interesting to note, Madam

        20       President, that when Article IV, Section 3 of

        21       the State Constitution was added -- the

        22       section was added which states "Senate

        23       only" -- in 1821, the reports of the

        24       proceedings and debates of the convention of



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         5433



         1       1821, assembled for the purpose of amending

         2       the Constitution of the State of New York,

         3       containing all the official documents relating

         4       to the subject and other valued materials.

         5                  It's also interesting to note,

         6       Madam President, that then Senator Martin Van

         7       Buren moved to insert the words "or the Senate

         8       only."  The amendment was supported by the

         9       mover upon the ground that it might be

        10       necessary for the Senate, with whom was lodged

        11       a part of the appointing power, to be convened

        12       without the other branch of the Legislature.

        13                  So if we were here just doing the

        14       job that we can only do as a Senate body, the

        15       appointing authority, it would probably be

        16       valid.  But if we are taking up legislation,

        17       we need the Assembly to be here as well for an

        18       extraordinary session.

        19                  ACTING PRESIDENT STEWART-COUSINS:

        20       Thank you, Senator Klein.

        21                  The ruling of the chair is that

        22       this Extraordinary Session Number 2 has not

        23       been noticed in conformity with applicable

        24       provisions of the New York State Constitution



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         5434



         1       and well-established parliamentary practice of

         2       this house.

         3                  Senator Smith.

         4                  SENATOR SMITH:    Yes, Madam

         5       President.  I rise, one, to appeal to our

         6       colleagues on the other side of the aisle.

         7       Obviously, this is no longer a time for us to

         8       do politics, this is more of a time for us to

         9       do work.

        10                  We are hoping that this

        11       Extraordinary Session Number 2,

        12       notwithstanding the legalities or the

        13       constitutionality of this session, that at

        14       least our colleagues on the other side of the

        15       aisle would show up for work.  Clearly, for

        16       them it's more about politics than it is about

        17       performing the people's business.

        18                  This is very important for us to

        19       show the people that we can rise above all of

        20       that.  Unfortunately, they have chose not to

        21       do that.

        22                  But notwithstanding that, Madam

        23       President, given -- in light of what my

        24       learned colleague Senator Klein has put forth,



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         5435



         1       Madam President, I ask that we would move to

         2       adjourn this body today and that we will not

         3       take up any business and we adjourn sine die.

         4                  ACTING PRESIDENT STEWART-COUSINS:

         5       Thank you, Senator Smith.

         6                  Being there is no further business

         7       to come before the Senate, on motion, the

         8       second extraordinary session is adjourned

         9       sine die.

        10                  (Whereupon, at 3:08 p.m., the

        11       Senate adjourned.)
